summary: Douglas County, OR, Umpqua NF lookout: L-4 cab from 1932-33, staffed 80 days in 1941, abandoned 1958 and gone; sources disagree on tower height.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a timber tower (sources give 20 ft or 10 ft)
facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1958 and gone; no source describes what remains at the site today.

staffing.status: Staffed for 80 days in 1941; reported to Steamboat Bridge Ranger Station

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Umpqua National Forest

events.note: Register gives 1932 as the build year for an L-4 cab on a 20-foot tower; a July 1932 newspaper report described it as planned
Forest Lookouts, citing Umpqua National Forest files, date the L-4 cab on a 10-foot timber tower to 1933
Several acres cleared to improve visibility from the lookout; the record tags the work as CCC
Staffed for 80 days and reported to the Steamboat Bridge Ranger Station

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Fire Lookout both give a 20-foot tower; the Forest Lookouts list, citing Umpqua National Forest files, gives a 10-foot timber tower. The sources do not settle it, so the facts omit height_m and the story reports both figures. The current record value of 3.0 m matches the 10-foot figure only.

The register gives 1932 as the build year and Fire Lookout gives 1934 for the tower. The Forest Lookouts list dates the L-4 cab to 1933 from Umpqua National Forest files, and its July 1932 item describes a planned build. The record keeps 1932 from the register and the story notes the 1933 date.

notes_for_editor: Abandonment in 1958 is backed by two sources (register and Fire Lookout), but the tower height and build year differ across sources and the story says so. The Forest Lookouts page is a summary of Umpqua National Forest files and Roseburg News-Review clippings, so the 1933 cab date has less independent support. Nothing we read describes the site today. Name clash: searches for Big Squaw Mountain return other peaks with the same name, so a reader may need the county to confirm they have the Oregon site.
